# A fixed bad cap contains every midpoint-supported residual centroid

This is an exact obstruction to a proposed selector, not a counterexample
to OC. It uses the already certified three-simplex body in
`candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`, whose other
middle-fiber points are not excluded by this note.

## 1. The body and the Brunn--Minkowski residual

Let B be the standard 5-simplex, of volume b=1/120 and centroid
g_B=(1/6,...,1/6). Use

    r=497/3000, R=9/2, ell=11/12-Rr, T=3979/6000,

and let D be the simplex with six vertices

    p=(0,11/12,0,0,0),
    b_0=(r,ell,0,0,0),
    b_i=b_0+T e_i, i=2,3,4,5.

These vertices belong to B, and D subset {x_1<=r}. Its relative volume is

    m=|D|/b=rT^4=124581095445185057/3888000000000000000,
    1/32<m<(11/20)^5<1.

Set q=m^(-1/5), A=(2-q)D and C=qD. Their relative volumes are

    a=|A|/b=(2m^(1/5)-1)^5 in (0,10^(-5)),
    |B|/b=|C|/b=1.

The actual ambient convex body is the convex hull of these fibers at
integer indices -1,0,1. Its midpoint inclusion is (A+C)/2=D subset B,
so the fibers are exactly A,B,C, and the total mixed volume is (2+a)b.
The body is full-dimensional and all three fibers have positive volume.

The Brunn--Minkowski lower volume of the endpoint midpoint is EXACTLY

    a_0=[(|A|^(1/5)+|C|^(1/5))/2]^5=|D|=mb.       (1)

Indeed the two positive homothety factors sum to two. Similarly

    (g_A+g_C)/2=g_D,
    (g_D)_1=5r/6=497/3600<1/6.                    (2)

The latter identity averages one vertex with first coordinate zero and
five vertices with first coordinate r. In fact the dominated midpoint
measure can be exactly ordinary volume on D: couple the endpoint points
(2-q)X and qX using uniform X in D, so their midpoint is X.

The proposed residual center is therefore the actual centroid of B\D:

    y_res=(g_B-m g_D)/(1-m) in B,
    (y_res)_1-1/6=103m/[3600(1-m)]>0.              (3)

There is no erroneous use of centroid additivity for arbitrary Minkowski
sums: (1)--(2) follow from the explicit homotheties.

## 2. One fixed cap covers a much larger residual selector family

In fact let eta be ANY measure with 0<=eta<=1_B dx supported in D, of mass
t b where 0<t<=m<1. Write g_eta for its centroid and define the residual
centroid

    y_eta=(g_B-t g_eta)/(1-t).

This is the centroid of the nonnegative positive-mass residual measure
1_B dx-eta, so it belongs to B. Because (g_eta)_1<=r<1/6,

    (y_eta)_1-1/6
       =[t/(1-t)](1/6-(g_eta)_1)>0.                (4)

Include g_B itself as the zero-mass case. Thus the convex hull of g_B and
ALL these residual centroids lies in {x_1>=1/6}. This family contains the
Brunn--Minkowski residual (3), its segment with g_B, and any residual
obtained from any dominated coupling output supported in the endpoint
midpoint body. It allows arbitrary fractional densities and masses;
neither a chosen coupling nor a convex support for eta is assumed.

Define the closed ambient cap

    H_1={(z,x): x_1+(1-q)r z>=h},
    h=1/6-(2/25)a.                                (5)

Its middle trace contains every point in the preceding convex hull,
including the closed boundary and g_B.

## 3. Exact sub-OC mass and endpoint failure

At either endpoint the maximum of the left side of (5) is exactly r:
at -1 it is (2-q)r-(1-q)r; at +1 it is qr+(1-q)r. Since
1/6-r=1/1000 and (2/25)a<1/1000, the threshold h is strictly larger
than r. Hence H_1 excludes BOTH endpoint fibers. Its whole mixed mass is
the standard-simplex cap in B:

    mu(H_1)/b=(1-h)^5
       =gamma_5[1+(12/125)a]^5,
    gamma_5=(5/6)^5.

The OC target is gamma_5(1+a/2). For 0<a<=1/100,

 ([1+(12/125)a]^5-1)/a
 <=(12/25)[1+(12/125)(1/100)]^4
 =1148810043113472/2384185791015625<1/2.

Our a is smaller than 10^(-5), so this proves

    mu(H_1)<(gamma_5/2)mu(S).                      (6)

Thus EVERY proposed residual center in Section 2, and every point of their
convex hull with g_B, has depth strictly less than gamma_5/2.

Every point in either endpoint fiber also fails this target. A simplex of
volume V has maximum own-fiber halfspace depth gamma_5 V: choose a largest
barycentric coordinate and its parallel vertex cap for the upper bound,
and use Grunbaum at the centroid for equality. Since each endpoint index
is extreme, that cap extends with a sufficiently large integer tilt to
exclude the other two compact fibers. The absolute mixed depths at the
endpoints are therefore at most gamma_5 a b and gamma_5 b, both strictly
below gamma_5(1+a/2)b.

Consequently adding deepest endpoint points to the entire residual family
does not repair this selector. The failure persists while all three fibers
are simplices and all are strictly below half the total volume. It does
not say that other points of B fail OC, and it does not negate the proved
residual own-fiber lower bound gamma_5(b-a_0).
